jobs.occupation: Head of P&O for Louis Nielsen
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about creating an exceptional employee experience and enabling business performance? Then this could be your next opportunity at Louis Nielsen and Specsavers.

Join us as our new Head of P&O for Louis Nielsen and take responsibility for a people agenda spanning two distinct parts of our business: our Support Office and our nationwide retail organisation. As a trusted business partner to the Country Leadership Team, you'll help shape organisational success by translating people priorities into meaningful business outcomes while leading a skilled, supportive and caring P&O team.

Your role

As Head of P&O, you will lead the local P&O team and people agenda for Louis Nielsen in Denmark. The role has two important dimensions.

For our Support Office, you will work closely with the Country Director and management team as a strategic P&O partner. You will help shape the organisation, leadership and employee experience needed to deliver the business plan, including organisational change, talent and performance, recruitment and onboarding, leadership development and engagement.

For our Retail organisation, you will ensure that the P&O team provides relevant and effective support to our stores and retail leaders. This includes strengthening the P&O services, processes and guidance available to stores, particularly within employee relations, employee experience and core people processes.

Across both areas, you will lead and develop the local P&O team, including payroll and connect Louis Nielsen with the wider Northern Europe P&O organisation, translating regional and global priorities into locally relevant delivery.

Your key responsibilities

Partnering with our Support Office:

• Partner with the Country Director and management team to shape and deliver the people agenda and local business plan.

• Advise and coach leaders on organisation, leadership, talent, performance and people-related matters.

• Lead organisational change and support leaders and colleagues through change.

• Ensure strong recruitment and onboarding, talent and performance processes, and development planning across the Support Office.

• Drive employee engagement, including Great Place to Work, action planning and follow-up.

Enabling our Retail organisation:

• Ensure that retail leaders and stores have access to relevant and effective P&O services and support.

• Support the continued development and delivery of HR services to stores, including employee relations and employee experience guidance.

• Ensure that core people processes and policies are practical, consistent and effective within our retail environment.

• Work closely with retail leadership to identify emerging people needs and translate them into appropriate P&O solutions.

Leading P&O and connecting with Northern Europe:

• Lead and develop the local P&O team, including payroll, creating clarity, capability and strong delivery.

• Represent Denmark within the Northern Europe P&O team and contribute to the Northern Europe People Plan.

• Translate relevant regional and global people priorities into strong local delivery.

• Partner with regional P&O colleagues across business partnering, learning and development, and operational excellence.

• Lead and contribute to cross-functional projects in Denmark and across Northern Europe.

Your new team

You'll lead the Danish People & Organisation team of six people while being part of the wider Northern Europe P&O function.

The team supports two distinct parts of Louis Nielsen: our Support Office and our nationwide retail organisation. The nature of that support differs, and an important part of your role will be ensuring that our P&O model meets the needs of both.

Within the Support Office, the team works closely with leaders and colleagues across the full employee lifecycle. For Retail, the focus is on providing scalable, effective P&O services, processes and guidance that enable our retail leaders and stores to succeed. You will also collaborate closely with colleagues across the Northern Europe P&O function.

What are we looking for?

“We are looking for someone who genuinely cares about our people, builds trust, and understands everyday life in our stores and Support Office. Someone who offers practical support and keeps things simple and efficient, freeing up time for meaningful conversations, development and looking ahead. You’ll help shape the people agenda in Denmark—and I look forward to working alongside you and our colleagues across Northern Europe, sharing ideas and supporting one another.”_

- Malene Green Brostrøm, People Director Northern Europe

Preferably our candidates will have some of the following competencies:

• Significant HR leadership experience within a complex, matrix organisation.

• Experience acting as a strategic People partner to senior business leaders.

• Experience balancing strategic business partnering with the delivery of scalable and effective HR services across different employee populations.

• A strong track record of leading organisational change and transformation initiatives.

• Experience linking business strategy, people priorities, and employee engagement outcomes.

• Experience working within an international environment.

• Excellent stakeholder management, communication, coaching, and influencing skills.

• Strong leadership experience with a proven ability to develop high-performing teams.

• The ability to move comfortably between strategic business partnering and ensuring strong, pragmatic P&O delivery.

It would be an advantage if you have:

• Experience within retail, consumer goods, or other customer-facing multi-site environments.

• Experience working across multiple countries or markets.

• Knowledge of employment relations and organisational change programmes.

• Experience leading cross-functional projects in an international organisation.

As a person, we believe that you are:

• An inspiring leader who develops and motivates others.

• A trusted advisor who builds credibility and strong relationships at all levels.

• Commercially minded and able to connect people priorities with business performance.

• Structured and resilient, with the ability to navigate complexity and change.

• A collaborative communicator who engages stakeholders across functions and geographies.

What awaits you upon joining Louis Nielsen

At Louis Nielsen and Specsavers, you'll get more than just a job. You'll join an organisation with a clear purpose: changing lives through better sight and hearing.

We offer an exciting and influential leadership role where you'll play a key part in shaping the future of our people agenda in Denmark.

Joining us, you’ll get:

• Competitive compensation and benefits.

• Significant exposure to senior business leaders and strategic decision-making.

• An international and collaborative work environment.

• The chance to make a meaningful impact on both people and business performance.

• A culture built on trust, inclusion, and continuous development.

Your base will be at Louis Nielsen’s Support Office in Aalborg, but we take a very flexible approach to where you work. Finding the right person matters more to us than where in Denmark you live. You should, however, expect to spend a couple of days in Aalborg each week.

Is this your next step? Then apply today

To apply, please send us your CV using the button below. We want to respect your time, so including an application letter is optional. Feel free to apply as soon as possible. Please avoid including any photos or references to your age in your CV. It contributes to a fairer and more unbiased assessment.

We review CVs and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis. Our recruitment process typically consists of an initial screening, two rounds of interviews, and a personality assessment feedback session.

About Celvivo

Celvivo is a Danish life science company developing innovative solutions for growing and studying cells in 3D while mimicking in vivo conditions. Our platform brings together advanced laboratory equipment and cloud-based software, helping researchers explore new possibilities in cell culture and achieve new results in their scientific research and their work towards better patient outcomes.

Celvivo has a team of 35 employees across Denmark, the United States, Sweden, the Netherlands, the UAE, and Singapore.

As we expand our presence within the pharmaceutical industry, we are looking for an experienced and entrepreneurial Director of Quality Assurance & Regulatory Affairs to establish and lead our quality and regulatory journey.

The Opportunity

You will play a central role in preparing Celvivo for increased engagement with pharmaceutical customers, ensuring that our quality systems, certifications, product compliance practices, and regulatory approach support both current and future business objectives.

You will report directly to our CEO and serve as a key member of the management team, defining and implementing Celvivo’s quality and regulatory strategy. Initially, you will be a hands-on leader working closely with external consultants to establish the foundations of the QA/RA function. As the company grows, you will build and develop the QA/RA agenda and capabilities required to support our future ambitions.

This is a unique opportunity to work with a premium product and shape the quality and regulatory strategy at an ambitious growth company, where your decisions will directly influence our future direction, customer relationships, and market opportunities.

What You Will Do

Quality & Regulatory Strategy

• Define Celvivo’s quality and regulatory roadmap, including recommendations regarding certifications, regulatory positioning, and quality investments.

• Advise executive management on strategic quality and regulatory decisions.

• Develop budgets and implementation plans for QA/RA initiatives.

Quality Management System & Certification

• Lead the implementation of a scalable Quality Management System.

• Establish SOP frameworks and key quality processes.

• Drive certification activities and ensure ongoing compliance.

Regulatory Affairs & Product Compliance

• Determine product classifications across key markets, including the EU and US.

• Ensure compliance of product claims, labeling, marketing materials, and CE marking activities.

• Monitor regulatory developments relevant to Celvivo and our customers.

Customer & Supplier Quality

• Serve as the primary quality contact for customers.

• Lead customer and supplier audits.

• Establish and maintain quality agreements with distributors, suppliers, and customers.

• Ensure audit readiness across the organization.

Leadership & Business Partnership

• Collaborate closely with colleagues across the organization to create a pragmatic and effective quality culture.

• Maintain external and internal key stakeholders.

• Contribute actively to the management team and overall company strategy.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, you will:

• 

• Complete a comprehensive gap analysis and recommend Celvivo’s future quality and regulatory path.

• Deliver an approved QA/RA roadmap and budget.

• Establish the SOP framework and document product classifications.

• Implement core QMS processes and prepare the company for certification.

• Develop a scalable resource plan for the future QA/RA organization

What You Bring

We imagine that you bring:

• 

• An MSc or equivalent degree in Life Sciences, Engineering, or a related discipline.

• More than 10 years of QA/RA experience within life science tools, medical devices, diagnostics, or pharmaceutical environments.

• A proven ability to influence senior stakeholders.

• Experience implementing ISO 9001 and/or ISO 13485 compliant quality management systems, ideally from the ground up.

• Experience driving certification activities and interacting with auditors.

• Strong knowledge of product classification, labeling, and compliance requirements for laboratory equipment and related technologies.

• Experience working with pharmaceutical customers and quality audits is highly advantageous.

• Excellent written and verbal English communication skills. Danish is considered a plus

Why Join Celvivo?

At Celvivo you have the right to be nerdy, the obligation to be friendly, the chance to be pioneering and the privilege of working with premium products. We combine scientific curiosity with entrepreneurial ambition, and we are united by our mission to help researchers achieve better outcomes through smarter ways of working.

As Director of QA/RA, you will have a rare opportunity to create a function from the ground up and make a tangible impact on Celvivo’s future growth and success together with a team of passionate colleagues.

Interested? Send us your CV and a cover letter with a few words about yourself, your experience, and what motivates you to join Celvivo.

Corti builds AI for critical industries. We started in healthcare, where messy inputs, specialized knowledge, and consequential errors make demanding engineering problems unavoidable. Today we train and post-train models, build agents, and turn research into APIs that developers use to build their products. Our platform supports more than one million production interactions every week.

We are building Europe’s alternative to closed AI: ambitious model development, published research, and AI infrastructure that gives developers control over the systems they depend on.

Our platform and APIs provide the building blocks for specialized intelligence that organizations own:

• 
Models: frontier and open-weight models with reasoning, tool calling, structured output, and embeddings through an OpenAI-compatible interface, plus custom models trained and post-trained on an organization’s own data.

• 
Sovereign compute: GPU capacity on Corti-operated European infrastructure for teams that need their data and workloads to stay in Europe.

• 
Agents: a harness to build, evaluate, and optimize agents that connect to real systems, with planning, tool use, external knowledge, persistent context, human approval, and observable execution.

• 
Speech: live dictation, conversational transcription, and batch audio processing.

• 
Clinical documentation: fact extraction as conversations unfold, and document generation with explicit schemas and controllable synthesis.

• 
Medical coding: code predictions from clinical narratives, linked to supporting passages.

Explore the platform at docs.corti.ai.

The Role

You want to train models at the frontier, and you want the science in the open, where other engineers can inspect it. At Corti, you don't have to choose.

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer in our Applied AI team, you drive large-scale training and post-training alongside researchers and engineers. Your decisions span the training recipe, the evaluation, and the system that serves the result. The calls are consequential, and you stay close enough to the implementation to understand why they succeed or fail.

What You Will Do

• 
Designing and running distributed training, including architecture, data pipelines, parallelism, checkpointing, evaluation, and recovery.

• 
Improving model capabilities through supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and distillation.

• 
Finding the causes of unstable training, inefficient communication, poor utilization, and unexpected regressions.

• 
Developing models for agentic work: choosing tools, using evidence, maintaining context, and completing complex tasks reliably.

• 
Building evaluations that expose failure modes and establish whether an improvement holds outside the training distribution, including LLM-as-judge systems you build and calibrate

• 
Creating and curating training data, including synthetic data pipelines that feed real training runs.

• 
Turning stronger models into practical APIs by improving latency, throughput, memory use, and serving cost.

Which capabilities belong in the weights, and which need tools or retrieval? You help decide, and you build the experiments that establish the answer.

Put the science where engineers can inspect it

We believe engineers should be able to examine the methods and evidence behind the systems they build on. We publish research, release benchmark resources, and document how our platform works. Read the work behind our clinical APIs: corti.ai/research

Who you are

You have depth and an urge to experiment

• 
You have trained large language models and owned technically complex ML work. You can explain a difficult run in detail: the architecture, the bottleneck, the failed hypothesis, and the evidence that changed your mind.

• 
You bring strong practical distributed-training experience, and depth in areas such as mixture-of-experts models, reinforcement learning, or distillation. Experience serving open-weight models is a plus. You write code other engineers can build on and make technical trade offs clear.

• 
You know post-training methods from the inside.Preference optimisation and reinforcement learning have quirks, reward hacking, runs that look stable until they collapse, and signals that turns out to be noise. You have hit these problems and learned to spot them before they cost you a week.

• 
You have hands-on experience with the data the models learn from. You have built training-data pipelines, ideally synthetic ones, and stayed close to the training that consumed your data.

• 
You have evaluated LLMs in production. You have built and calibrated LLM-as-judge systems to automate that evaluation, and you know when a judge's score means something and when it just flatters the model it is scoring.

• 
You also have the itch to investigate. A new model, paper, or agent framework appears, and you want to understand what actually changed. You build experiments, compare approaches, and test the claims. Perhaps your latest side project involves agents building tools, coordinating with other agents, or failing in a surprisingly instructive way. We want to hear about it.

• 
A relevant advanced degree is welcome; equivalent experience matters just as much.

Build with us in Copenhagen

This is a full-time role reporting to the CTO. We provide equipment and relocation support.

We welcome different backgrounds and paths into machine learning. If the work fits your ambition and you bring substantial relevant experience, apply even if you do not match every item.

Send us something you built, a hard problem you solved, or a result you think deserves to be challenged. A link is enough. Help us shape the models, agents, and infrastructure developers build on next.

Additionally, we want to remind you that experience comes in many forms, and we're passionate about creating teams with a multitude of perspectives! If you believe your experience is close to what we're looking for but not an exact match, we still hope you consider applying!

Joining our QA & Product Compliance department here in Sønderborg, you’ll work closely with engineers, other technical specialists, our in-house test center, and external testing laboratories. **About us:

**Founded in Copenhagen, Denmark, in 2014, Templafy’s success is built by our 60+ employee nationalities found at offices around the world. We believe that when people feel valued, heard, and empowered, they perform at their best—creating a win for all. Our unique product and dedication to innovation and excellence have raised over $200 million in funding from top investors like Insight Venture Partners, Seed Capital, Dawn Capital, Damgaard Company and Golub Capital.

Role Summary

As Corporate Security Engineer at Templafy, you will help secure the corporate technology foundation of a global SaaS company building AI-powered document generation and business content solutions. You will take responsibility for protecting the systems, identities, devices, networks, and SaaS platforms that enable our teams to operate securely at scale.

This is a hands-on engineering role where you will design and operate controls across identity, endpoints, email, data protection, cloud, and SaaS governance. As a technical security partner, you will contribute to corporate infrastructure decisions and help shape how Templafy protects its business operations as the company grows.

You will collaborate closely with IT, Security, Legal, Privacy, and business stakeholders. A separate Senior Information Security Analyst is responsible for application and product security and incident response. This role complements that work by strengthening the corporate environment that supports the wider business.

What Will Help You Succeed

You have experience in corporate or infrastructure security and enjoy building, hardening, automating, and continuously improving systems.

You use sound judgment to assess risk, make pragmatic technical decisions, and determine when broader input is needed. You are comfortable working across technical and non-technical teams and can translate security requirements into practical solutions that people can understand and adopt.

You enjoy improving systems through automation, scripting, and thoughtful workflow design. You are comfortable taking responsibility for security initiatives while collaborating with colleagues when decisions require broader input. You will have the opportunity to work across several technical areas and help shape our corporate security practices as our technology and business evolve.

Key Responsibilities

• Identity and access security — Design and operate controls across the identity layer, including JIT/PAM, Conditional Access, OAuth scope reviews, and SSO enforcement.

• Endpoint and platform security — Implement and operate the Microsoft 365 Defender suite, harden endpoints, and manage patching and remediation across Windows, macOS, and corporate applications.

• Data protection — Implement and manage data loss prevention controls and configure backup solutions, such as Keepit, for corporate and SaaS data.

• Network and email security — Deploy and maintain firewalls, egress filtering, network segmentation, anti-phishing controls, and email authentication standards including DMARC, DKIM, and SPF.

• SaaS governance — Discover and govern shadow IT and unsanctioned SaaS or AI usage, and support effective application patching and lifecycle management.

• Security automation — Automate routine IT and security operations, including lifecycle workflows, compliance checks, access reviews, asset discovery, and data classification. Build scripting-based tools using PowerShell or Python and use appropriate automation and agentic tooling to improve manual workflows.

• Security advisory — Partner with the IT Administrator on security-related decisions, provide technical input on vendor assessments and integration reviews, and advise teams across the business on infrastructure security.

• Incident support — Investigate incidents involving corporate infrastructure in coordination with the Senior Information Security Analyst.

**Required Qualifications

**

• Relevant experience in corporate security engineering, infrastructure security, or a combined IT and security role, typically gained through four or more years of professional experience.

• Experience taking responsibility for at least one security domain—such as identity, endpoint, network, or data protection—from design and implementation through to ongoing operation and improvement.

• Practical experience implementing and operating an enterprise identity provider, including Conditional Access, privileged access controls, SSO, and MFA. Experience with Entra ID is preferred, but experience with platforms such as Okta or an equivalent solution is also relevant.

• Production experience implementing and operating at least one of the following: data loss prevention, network segmentation, or egress filtering.

• The ability to assess risk, evaluate trade-offs, and make clear, defensible prioritisation decisions.

• Scripting and automation skills using PowerShell, Python, or a comparable language, with examples of improving or replacing manual workflows.

• Experience scoping, coordinating, and delivering security projects involving multiple teams or business functions.

• Experience communicating security decisions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Experience working in a technology-led or similarly complex environment. Familiarity with B2B SaaS is beneficial but not essential.

**Preferred Qualifications

**

• Certifications such as CISSP, GSEC, Azure Security Engineer Associate, or equivalent knowledge developed through practical experience.

• Familiarity with security and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, or NIST CSF.

• Experience with SaaS backup solutions such as Keepit, Veeam, or an equivalent platform.

• Private health insurance

• Company lunch contribution

• Phone and broadband covered by company

• Centrally located office – easy access to public transportation

• Company events and team activities

• Flexible work environment

jobs.occupation: PhD in modelling and experiments on PEM electrolysis
jobs.description:
At the Faculty of Engineering and Science, AAU Energy, a position as PhD stipend is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from January 1st or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

Your work tasks

The position is offered in relation to the research group "Hydrogen and Electro Fuels" and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for “Thermal Engineering”.

Your competencies As a PhD student in modelling and experiments on PEM water electrolysis, you will work at the intersection of chemical and electrochemical reactor engineering, with a particular emphasis on electrolysis. The project focuses on testing proton exchange membrane electrolysis cells, characterising their electrochemical performance and developing detailed electrochemical cell models. You will design and carry out experiments on single cells, analyse electrochemical behaviour under different operating conditions and use the resulting data to build, calibrate and validate mechanistic models that describe transport, kinetics and degradation phenomena.

An important part of your work will be to investigate how PEM electrolysers perform when conventional materials are partially replaced by recycled ionomers and iridium. You will compare performance, stability and degradation patterns with and without recycled components and translate your findings into a deeper understanding of the underlying electrochemical mechanisms. In parallel, you will conduct techno‑economic assessments of PEM electrolysis systems, including related life cycle assessment studies, to evaluate how material choices, operating strategies and system design affect costs and environmental impacts over the full life cycle.

The PhD project is carried out in the context of the CYCLOPEM, EDSOES and CAPEX projects, which provide access to state‑of‑the‑art experimental facilities and collaboration with academic and industrial partners. You are expected to participate in project meetings and to present your results at international conferences and workshops. In addition, you will contribute to teaching activities within courses on chemical and electrochemical reactors and take part in the daily activities of the Hydrogen and Electro Fuels research group at AAU Energy, including group meetings, seminars and joint publications.

The applicant must have a relevant professional and/or educational background within thermal, chemical and electrochemical engineering. Modelling of chemical and electrochemical reactor and LCA.

**Qualification requirements

**PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

**Who we are

**AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean

and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real‑world energy challenges.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg/Esbjerg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday life. New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters.

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

**How to apply

**Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades)

• Project description (4-5 pages), that: describes the applicant’s initial thoughts and ideas related to the specific project applied for. This includes a brief state-of-the-art (including short list of references), a time schedule and how the applicant intends to shed light on the project objectives

• Other relevant documents

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.

Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

**Salary and terms of employment

**The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement).

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

You’ll work in an international head office with a collaborative, open culture—where ideas matter, and impact is visible. jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Molecular Plant-Microbe Interactions
jobs.description:
The Plant Molecular Biology section at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics is seeking a highly motivated and ambitious postdoctoral researcher to join a dynamic and international research team. You will play a central role in advancing our understanding of the molecular dialogue between plants and their associated microorganisms, with the long-term goal of contributing to more sustainable and resilient agricultural systems.

The research team you will join is coordinating an international program that brings together leading scientists from around the world to investigate beneficial plant–microbe associations and harness their potential for sustainable food production.

Our focus is on uncovering the molecular mechanisms by which plants and microbes interact—ranging from early recognition events to colonization strategies. Within this framework, the advertised postdoctoral project is specifically focused on plant engineering for improved symbiotic associations with soil microbes. This knowledge forms the foundation for the development of novel solutions to reduce the need for chemical inputs and improve crop productivity, particularly in smallholder farming systems.

Your contributions will directly support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially those related to food security, sustainability, and climate resilience.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a fixed-term position from 15 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, to end on 31 March 2028.

Job description
• Conduct independent and collaborative research into the molecular and genetic basis of plant–microbe interactions, with a particular emphasis on beneficial symbioses.
• Design, execute, and analyze experiments using molecular biology, plant transformation, gene expression, and phenotyping.
• Apply plant genetics and genomics to study mechanisms underlying plant–associated bacteria.
• Collaborate with international partners and contribute to joint research efforts within the program.
• Present your work at group meetings, conferences, and in high-quality scientific publications.
• Contribute to the supervision of MSc and PhD students, fostering an inclusive and supportive research environment.
Your profile
• You hold a PhD in Molecular Biology, Plant Biology, or a related field.
• You have strong expertise in molecular and genetic techniques, with prior experience in plant genetics and molecular biology.
• Experience working with plant–microbe systems will be considered an advantage.
• Expertise in genetic engineering, transcriptomics, or advanced microscopy will also be an asset.
• You are curious, creative, and capable of driving projects independently while thriving in collaborative research settings.
• You have excellent communication skills and are fluent in English, both spoken and written.
• You are motivated to contribute to applied outcomes of fundamental research in support of sustainable agriculture.
Who we are
The postdoctoral researcher will be affiliated with the Plant Molecular Biology section at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University, where the research program is coordinated.

The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics is part of the Faculty of Natural Sciences and encompasses research within Plant Molecular Biology, Neurobiology, RNA Biology and Innovation, Protein Science, Cellular Health, Intervention and Nutrition. The department currently hosts 158 full-time scientific staff and 83 PhD students. It also delivers two degree programs: Molecular Biology and Molecular Medicine, with an annual intake of ~120 students.

For more information, please visit:

http://mbg.au.dk/ – Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics

https://nat.au.dk/ – Faculty of Natural Sciences

http://www.au.dk/ – Aarhus University

What we offer 
• A full-time position.
• A role in an ambitious, research-intensive environment with strong international collaborations.
• The opportunity to pursue high-impact research in plant–microbe interactions with both fundamental and applied dimensions.
• A collaborative and respectful work culture that values diversity, creativity, and professional growth.
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Universitetsbyen 81, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. The area of employment is Aarhus University with affiliated institutions.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Professor Simona Radutoiu, radutoiu@mbg.au.dk

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 7 December 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.
